name: BNN-20

lead: BNN-20 is a lab-made steroid-like compound, described by its developers as a "microneurotrophin", meant to mimic the brain growth factor BDNF. People in research-chemical circles discuss it for brain protection and cognitive support.

It is derived from DHEA, crosses the blood-brain barrier and is reported to lack endocrine side effects. It acts through the TrkB receptor and reduces neuroinflammation in mouse models, mainly the "weaver" mouse model of Parkinson's-like dopamine neuron loss. No human studies exist and no appearance use is documented.

paras: It is discussed in longevity and nootropic circles as a neurotrophin mimic. There is no established human routine or timeline.
Human safety is unknown because no clinical trials are published. It is not an approved drug.

angle.text: BNN-20 is a DHEA-derived BDNF mimic discussed in research-chemical circles for brain protection and cognitive support. No appearance use is documented; the research is preclinical, mainly Parkinson's mouse models.

lead: BNN-20 is a synthetic compound described by its developers as a "microneurotrophin": a small molecule, 17-beta-spiro-[5-androsten-17,2'-oxiran]-3beta-ol, derived from the hormone DHEA, that crosses the blood-brain barrier and is reported to lack endocrine side effects. [1]

Research has been preclinical, mainly in the "weaver" mouse model of Parkinson's-like dopamine neuron loss. [1][2][3] It is discussed in longevity and nootropic circles as a neurotrophin mimic; it has no approved use.

paras: In weaver mice, BNN-20 was reported to protect dopaminergic neurons through the TrkB neurotrophin receptor. [1] Follow-up studies reported protection when treatment began at an advanced stage, reduced neuroinflammation, and effects on neurogenesis in the substantia nigra. [2][3][4]
No studies found. Published research is limited to cell cultures and mouse models, including work on grafted neural progenitors. [1][2][3][5]

timeline.event: Neuroprotection of dopaminergic neurons in the weaver mouse reported. [1]
Anti-neuroinflammatory effects reported at advanced degeneration. [3]
Effects on substantia nigra neurogenesis reported. [2]
